gloss: Shinto ritual prayer (recited by a priest)

definitions.gloss: Shinto ritual prayer; formal address to the kami
definitions.explanation: A set text chanted aloud by a Shinto priest at ceremonies — ground-breaking rites, shrine festivals, weddings, purifications — reporting the occasion to the deity and asking for protection. Composed in an archaic, highly formal style of Japanese.

examples.japanese: {神主|かんぬし}が{祝詞|のりと}をあげる。
examples.english: The Shinto priest recites the ritual prayer.

examples.japanese: {地鎮祭|じちんさい}で{祝詞|のりと}が{読|よ}み{上|あ}げられた。
examples.english: A ritual prayer was read aloud at the ground-breaking ceremony.

examples.japanese: {神前|しんぜん}{結婚式|けっこんしき}では、{神主|かんぬし}が{二人|ふたり}の{名|な}を{読|よ}み{上|あ}げて{祝詞|のりと}を{奏上|そうじょう}する。
examples.english: At a Shinto wedding, the priest reads out the couple's names and offers the ritual prayer to the deity.

notes:
Heard by most Japanese people at least a few times in life — at a shrine visit for a child's blessing, a wedding, or a construction ground-breaking.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {祝詞|のりと}をあげる: to recite a ritual prayer (everyday phrasing)
- {祝詞|のりと}を{奏上|そうじょう}する: to offer the prayer to the deity (formal phrasing)
- {祝詞|のりと}を{読|よ}み{上|あ}げる: to read the prayer aloud

READING NOTE:
The same characters read しゅくし mean a written congratulatory address delivered at a ceremony — a different word entirely.
